:::: course-main
## About this course

Turn RStudio into your Geographic Information System. This hands-on course takes you from "what is spatial data?" to publishing your own interactive web maps, using the packages that power GIS in R today: `sf`, `terra`, `ggplot2` and `mapview`.

Every topic is taught in two steps. A short **theory** lesson (with a quiz) explains the concepts, and a **practice** lesson applies them to real data, step by step. Each block ends with a **challenge**, a set of proposed exercises to test what you've learned on your own.

You'll work with vector and raster data, master coordinate reference systems, run spatial joins and geometry operations, compute terrain derivatives and vegetation indices like NDVI, and finish by building five complete maps, from population in Spain to wildfire severity in Tenerife, both as static figures and as web maps.

::: course-video
{{< video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FSE_VnJuTFw aspect-ratio="16x9" >}}
:::

## What you'll learn

```{r}
course_checklist(c(
  "Use the essential R packages for GIS: `sf`, `terra`, `ggplot2` and `mapview`",
  "Download, import and export vector and raster data straight from R",
  "Understand, assign and transform coordinate reference systems (CRS)",
  "Filter, join and measure features with spatial predicates and operations",
  "Crop, reclassify and do map algebra with rasters and elevation models",
  "Compute vegetation indices such as NDVI and build false-color composites",
  "Design publication-ready static maps with `ggplot2`",
  "Publish interactive web maps, including synchronized and side-by-side views"
))
```

## Who this course is for

```{r}
course_checklist(c(
  "GIS users (QGIS, ArcGIS) who want reproducible, scriptable workflows in R",
  "Ecologists, foresters, geographers and environmental scientists working with maps",
  "Data analysts who know some R and want to add the spatial dimension",
  "Students and researchers who need to analyze and map spatial data for their projects"
), columns = 1)
```

## Requirements

```{r}
course_checklist(c(
  "Basic knowledge of R",
  "Some familiarity with the `tidyverse` (the pipe and basic `ggplot2` plots) is recommended"
), columns = 1)
```

No previous GIS experience is needed: spatial concepts are explained from scratch.

## Course contents

```{r}
course_data <- list(

      "Course materials"

  list(

    topics = c(
      "Importance of CRS",
      "CRS, coordinates, georeferencing",

      "EPSG codes, proj4, WKT..."

  ),
  list(
    title = "Unit 3b - Coordinate Reference Systems (Practice)",
    topics = c(
      "Exploring CRS",
      "CRS transformation",
      "CRS assignment",
      "On-the-fly transformations",
      "Web maps",
      "CHALLENGE 02 - proposed exercises"
    )
  ),
  list(
    title = "Unit 4a - Geometry Operations (Theory)",
    topics = c(
      "Spatial predicates",
      "Geometry measurements",
      "Unary transformations",
      "Binary transformations",
      "Other operations"
    )
  ),
  list(
    title = "Unit 4b - Geometry Operations (Practice)",

      "Predicate functions",

      "Spatial joins",
```
